title: Apostille for Vietnam: degree and documents (2026)
description: Vietnam has accepted apostilles since 11 Sep 2026: which papers need one, each country's route, the exceptions, Saigon translations and the 6-month trap.
h1: Getting your degree and documents authenticated for Vietnam: apostille, legalisation and translation
intro: Since 11 September 2026 Vietnam accepts apostilles: if your degree, police check and other papers come from a member country that did not object, including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa and the Philippines, one apostille from that country replaces Vietnamese-embassy legalisation. German, Austrian and Czech documents, and Thai ones until 28 February 2027, still need consular legalisation. Either way, each document also needs a Vietnamese translation certified under Vietnamese law.
keyPoints: Since **11 September 2026**, one apostille from the issuing country replaces the old notarise-authenticate-legalise chain for documents from the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, the Philippines and every other member that did not object (Decree 293/2026/ND-CP).
Germany, Austria and Czechia objected, and Thailand joins only on 28 February 2027: documents **issued** in those countries still go through consular legalisation, whatever your nationality.

An apostille does not replace translation. Every document needs a Vietnamese translation with the **translator's signature certified** at a ward People's Committee or a notary office; the old 'notarised translation' was abolished on 1 July 2025.

Authenticate your degree, your home-country criminal record, experience letters from employers abroad and your TEFL, TESOL or CELTA certificate. Private papers (letters, private course certificates) need a notary or solicitor before the apostille.
The criminal record must be issued **no more than 6 months before the employer files** your work permit. The clock runs from the issue date, not the apostille date, so order it last.

blocks.text: Vietnam acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention on 31 December 2025 and the Convention entered into force for it on **11 September 2026** ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41)). [Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://datafiles.chinhphu.vn/cpp/files/vbpq/2026/7/293_2026_nd-cp_23072026_1-signed.signed.pdf), signed on 23 July 2026, implements it. A public document from a country the Convention applies to, carrying a valid apostille, can now be used in Vietnam without consular legalisation, and Vietnamese offices may not demand legalisation on top of it (Art. 25).

Before that date every foreign document went through a chain: notarise where needed, authenticate at the home foreign ministry, then legalise at the Vietnamese embassy. For apostille countries that chain is over: Vietnamese embassies and consulates stopped legalising those documents on 11 September 2026, as the [Vietnamese Embassy in the USA](https://vietnamembassy-usa.org/news/2026/09/notice-application-apostille-place-consular-legalisation-11-september-2026) confirms. An agent's quote that still includes a 'Vietnamese embassy attestation' step for a US, UK, Canadian, Australian, Irish, New Zealand, South African or Philippine document is out of date.

blocks.text: The route follows the country that **issued** the document, not your passport. A Canadian with a German master's degree apostilles the Canadian police check and legalises the German degree; a TEFL certificate issued by a course provider in Thailand needs legalisation until 28 February 2027. The [HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs notice](https://mofahcm.gov.vn/so-ngoai-vu-thanh-pho-ho-chi-minh/thong-bao-ve-viec-tiep-nhan-ho-so-de-nghi-chung-nhan-apostilletai-bo-ngoai-giao) also warns that the UK's overseas territories, the Netherlands' overseas territories, Hong Kong and Macau issue apostilles separately, so the apostille must come from the territory where the document was issued. Some summaries list only two objecting states, or wrongly call Thailand an objector; the [HCCH notifications](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/notifications/?csid=1557&disp=type) are the authority.
Old paperwork still counts. Documents legalised before 11 September 2026 stay valid, and apostilles issued before that date by relationship states are accepted (Decree 293 Art. 36).

Teachers are filed as 'experts' under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/CongBaoCP/VanBan/2025/8/45798/58141-1-20251073-1074219-2025-nd-cp.pdf), in force since 7 August 2025, which needs a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant experience. Its Art. 5 says every foreign document in the dossier must be legalised unless a treaty exempts it (the apostille is that exemption), then translated into Vietnamese and certified. The full dossier is in [the work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers); these are the papers that come from abroad.

blocks.text: **Experience letters.** The usual proof of your 2 years is a letter from a past employer abroad stating your years of experience; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits (Decree 219 Art. 19). For experts in education, Art. 19(3) also lists documents showing you meet the qualification standard set by education law, but how Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is not published. If that is you, ask the employer which proof it will file and get the answer in writing before you travel. Never use a letter that is not true: an employer filing altered or forged documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-60000000}} ({{vnd:80000000-120000000}} for a company, school or centre) under [Decree 283/2026](https://kienthuc.net.vn/tu-1092026-phat-nang-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-khong-co-giay-phep-post1630701.html).

**The TEFL certificate** does not replace the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience in the work-permit test; it meets the education-side rule (Circular 21/2018 asks foreign teachers at language centres for a 'suitable' teaching certificate), and the law sets no minimum hours. Ho Chi Minh City checks the apostilled or legalised degree and teaching certificate with certified translations: in January 2026 the city's Department of Education [reviewed foreign teachers in public-school joint programmes](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html) and flagged those who held only course-completion certificates. More in [TEFL, TESOL or CELTA for Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam).

**Not on the list.** A health certificate from home is accepted only where Vietnam has a mutual-recognition agreement with that country, so in practice the health check is done in Vietnam; do not pay to authenticate one. Recognition of your degree by the Ministry of Education is not a work-permit item either (see the questions below).

sections.title: The apostille route, step by step

items.title: Get the version of each document the apostille office will take
items.text: Apostilles cover public documents only: police records, degrees and transcripts, notarial acts. Private papers such as an experience letter or a private TEFL certificate first become public through a notary or solicitor in the issuing country ([GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/get-document-legalised); Decree 293 Art. 3). Ask for paper originals where needed: the AFP hard copy, the Garda certificate with its wet-ink stamp, the original SAPS clearance. Do not laminate anything.

items.title: Have the issuing country apostille it
items.text: Only the competent authority of the country (or territory) that issued the document can apostille it; the country table below lists who that is. Your own embassy in Vietnam usually cannot help: British posts cannot legalise documents of any kind, and Irish embassies cannot issue apostilles. Australians are the exception worth asking about, because DFAT accepts documents lodged at Australian embassies and consulates abroad.

items.title: Skip the Vietnamese embassy
items.text: No Vietnamese stamp is needed on top of a valid apostille. Do not pay an agent for that step.

items.title: Bring the originals to Ho Chi Minh City
items.text: Keep the apostilled originals safe and work from certified copies. Since 1 November 2025 any ward People's Committee can certify copies of foreign-issued documents, wherever you live ([LSVN](https://lsvn.vn/tu-01-11-2025-ubnd-cap-xa-chung-thuc-cac-loai-giay-to-nao-a165222.html)). Decree 219 requires a copy to be certified against the original before it is translated.

items.title: Translate, including the apostille page
items.text: Have the translation made after the apostille, so it covers the apostille page too, and have the translator's signature certified (next section).

items.title: Hand the set to your employer
items.text: The employer, not you, is the applicant. It files online on the National Public Service Portal or at a Public Administration Service Centre, 60 to 10 days before your start date.

Police checks have their own guide: [criminal record check for a Vietnam work permit](/teach-in-vietnam/criminal-record-check-for-a-vietnam-work-permit).

**e-Apostilles.** Decree 293 gives a foreign e-Apostille the same legal value as a paper one, but how the Ho Chi Minh City work-permit office handles them in practice is not documented yet. Before you order one (a UK e-Apostille, or the electronic apostille that now comes with a Philippine CHED eCAV, which is reportedly invalid once printed), ask your employer whether it can file it.

sections.title: The legalisation route: Germany, Austria, Czechia and Thailand

blocks.text: Where the apostille does not apply, the old chain under Decree 111/2011, as amended by Decree 196/2025, still runs. It also covers documents outside the Convention, such as anything certified by a diplomatic or consular officer.

items.title: Notarise, if the document needs it
items.text: Copies and private papers are notarised in the issuing country first.

items.title: Certification by the home authority
items.text: The issuing country's competent authority, usually its foreign ministry, certifies the document.

items.title: Legalisation by Vietnam
items.text: The Vietnamese embassy or consulate in that country legalises it; it sets its own fees and times, so ask it. Alternatively, your country's mission in Vietnam certifies the document and then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Consular Department in Hanoi or the [HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs](https://mofahcm.gov.vn/hoi-dap) legalises it, for {{vnd:30000}} a copy.

items.title: Translate and certify in Vietnam
items.text: As on the apostille route, the Vietnamese translation comes last.

blocks.text: Legalisation inside Vietnam is quick once the document is in order: [Decree 196/2025](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/nghi-dinh-so-196-2025-nd-cp-sua-doi-bo-sung-quy-dinh-ve-chung-nhan-lanh-su-hop-phap-hoa-lanh-su-119250706205756884.htm) allows 1 working day for 1–4 documents, up to 2 for 5–9 and up to 4 for 10 or more. The HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs is at 6 Alexandre de Rhodes, Phường Sài Gòn; since July 2025 official addresses use the new ward names, not the old districts. Czech documents have one open point: Decree 293 gives priority to any treaty with simpler rules, so before paying for legalisation, ask the HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs whether a Vietnam–Czech agreement exempts yours.

sections.title: Certified translation and copies in Ho Chi Minh City

blocks.text: An apostille never replaces the translation: Decree 293 Art. 27 requires a Vietnamese translation, notarised or certified under Vietnamese law, for every apostilled document not in Vietnamese. Since 1 July 2025 notaries no longer 'notarise translations' (công chứng bản dịch). Instead, the **translator's signature is certified** (chứng thực chữ ký người dịch) at a ward or commune People's Committee or at a notary office ([Nhân Dân](https://nhandan.vn/nhieu-quy-dinh-moi-ve-cong-chung-post892108.html); [LSVN](https://lsvn.vn/tham-quyen-moi-cua-cap-xa-phuong-ke-tu-01-7-2025-a159699.html)). Translations notarised before that date stay valid.

blocks.text: Fees: the translation is priced by the translator or agency, so ask for a written quote per document that shows the translation and the certification separately. The [state fees at a ward](https://baochinhphu.vn/cach-tinh-phi-chung-thuc-ban-sao-tu-ban-chinh-102240527120026635.htm) are small: {{vnd:2000}} a page for a certified copy ({{vnd:1000}} a page from page 3, capped at {{vnd:200000}} a copy) and {{vnd:10000}} to certify a signature on one document, under Circular 226/2016/TT-BTC, as reported in 2024; confirm the fee at the counter. Agree with your school, in writing, who pays for translations and service fees; in practice teachers commonly pay for their own home-country documents, and the {{vnd:600000}} work-permit fee itself is the employer's. See [what to check in a teaching contract](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

Order matters: apostille or legalisation first, then a certified copy if you are filing a copy, then the translation, then certification of the translator's signature. Translating first leaves the apostille page untranslated, a rejection cause that legalisation agents report.

blocks.text: Add courier time both ways. Practitioner guides report one to six months from first document to issued permit, most of it spent gathering and authenticating documents at home. In Ho Chi Minh City the permit is issued by the Department of Home Affairs (Sở Nội vụ) for employers outside export-processing zones, industrial parks and high-tech parks, which covers practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html)). For the whole sequence from job offer to first class, see [how to become an English teacher in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/how-to-become-an-english-teacher-in-vietnam).

blocks.title: The 6-month clock starts on the issue date
blocks.text: Decree 219 Art. 18 accepts a criminal record from your home country or from Vietnam, but it must be **issued no more than 6 months before the employer files** the dossier. The clock runs from the date printed on the certificate, not from the apostille and not from your start date. Apostille queues and couriers regularly push a check past the limit, so do the degree and letters first and order the police check last, timed backwards from the filing date your employer gives you. UK providers suggest ordering it 8–10 weeks before you need it.

Already living in Vietnam? A Vietnamese criminal record also satisfies the decree. It is issued by the city police, not the Department of Justice (Sở Tư pháp), at counters including 161 Nguyễn Du, phường Bến Thành ([Tuổi Trẻ](https://tuoitre.vn/cong-an-tp-hcm-thay-doi-dia-diem-tiep-nhan-va-tra-ket-qua-ly-lich-tu-phap-20260213171448319.htm)), for {{vnd:200000}}, normally within [5 working days since 1 July 2026](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/tu-1-7-thoi-han-cap-phieu-ly-lich-tu-phap-5-ngay-lam-viec-119260403092607993.htm); the employer can also request it online together with the work permit. The law sets no minimum stay before a foreigner can ask for one, but how the city treats a Vietnamese record for someone who has only just arrived is not published, so ask your employer which record it will file.

sections.title: Why documents get rejected, and how to avoid it

items: **Expired police check**: issued more than 6 months before the filing date.

**Wrong copy type**: a plain photocopy that was never certified against the original (Decree 219 Art. 5 requires that before translation); the AFP PDF instead of the hard copy; a laminated certificate; an FBI report sent to a state Secretary of State instead of the US Department of State. Vendors also report that notarising an FBI report before the federal apostille can make it ineligible.

**A consulate-certified copy with an apostille**: a degree copy certified by your own embassy or consulate in Vietnam falls outside the Convention. A Vietnamese office can refuse it even with an apostille (Decree 293 Art. 26), and it stays on the legalisation track.

**Wrong route**: an apostille alone on a German, Austrian or Czech document, or on a Thai-issued certificate before 28 February 2027; an apostille from the wrong territory (UK overseas territories, the Netherlands' overseas territories, Hong Kong, Macau).

**Name mismatches**: your name must be spelled the same on the passport, degree, police check, TEFL certificate and experience letters. If your name changed, authenticate the marriage certificate or deed poll as well.
**Translation problems**: translating before the apostille, or asking a Vietnamese office for a 'notarised translation', a service that no longer exists.

**A defective apostille**: Decree 293 Art. 26 lets an office refuse an apostille that shows signs of alteration, was not issued by the competent authority, lacks the French title 'Apostille (Convention de La Haye du 5 octobre 1961)', or has been revoked.

blocks.text: Expect some friction in the first months of the new system. No Ho Chi Minh City notice yet describes how the work-permit office handles apostilles day to day, although the legal duty to accept them is clear. Bring originals plus scans, and if an officer is unsure, point to the issuing country's online apostille register or the QR code on the apostille, which Decree 293 Art. 27 allows offices to use for checking. Refusals must come in writing with reasons (Decree 219 Art. 22), and your employer, who files the dossier, has the final word on what it needs from you.

sections.title: After the permit: keep your originals

blocks.text: You will need the degree and experience proof again. A permit runs for up to 2 years and can be extended once by up to 2 years, then a new permit is needed; changing employer, even for the same job, also needs a new permit, and since [Decision 346/QĐ-BNV](https://www.ey.com/en_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/decision-346-qd-bnv-on-the-amendment-and-supplementation-of-administrative-procedures-for-foreign-employees-working-in-vietnam) (24 March 2026) you re-submit your degree and experience proof in those cases. Keep the apostilled originals and certified translations together, with scans, for every renewal or job change.

Going the other way works too: since 11 September 2026 the HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs apostilles Vietnamese documents for use abroad, such as a Vietnamese criminal record for your next job, for {{vnd:30000}} a copy, usually in 1 working day for 1–4 documents ([DOFA notice](https://mofahcm.gov.vn/so-ngoai-vu-thanh-pho-ho-chi-minh/thong-bao-ve-viec-tiep-nhan-ho-so-de-nghi-chung-nhan-apostilletai-bo-ngoai-giao)). More in [leaving Vietnam: a checklist](/teach-in-vietnam/leaving-vietnam-checklist-for-teachers).

faqs.q: My documents were legalised by the Vietnamese embassy before September 2026. Are they still valid?
faqs.a: Yes. Decree 293/2026/ND-CP keeps documents legalised before 11 September 2026 valid, and offices may not ask you to apostille them again. Apostilles issued before that date by relationship countries are also accepted. The criminal record still has to meet the 6-month rule on the filing date.

faqs.q: Do I need my degree recognised by Vietnam's Ministry of Education for a work permit?
faqs.a: No. Ministry recognition of a foreign degree is not an item in the Decree 219 work-permit dossier; the city checks the apostilled or legalised degree with a certified translation. Recognition is a separate procedure under Circular 65/2026/TT-BGDĐT, in force since 26 September 2026, which takes 20 working days, or 30 if the foreign institution must be verified.

faqs.q: Do I apostille the original degree or a copy?
faqs.a: It depends on the issuing country. The UK wants the degree certified by a solicitor or notary first, Ireland a solicitor- or notary-certified copy, Australia a university-verified degree or a notarised copy, and South Africa a verification letter or a High Court apostille on a notarised copy. In Vietnam you then file a ward-certified copy of the apostilled document, so the original stays with you.

faqs.q: Can I get my documents apostilled while I am already in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Only the issuing country's authority can apostille, so documents usually go home by post or through an agent. British posts cannot legalise anything; Australians can ask the Consulate-General in Ho Chi Minh City whether it can lodge an apostille request with DFAT. A copy certified by your own consulate here is not apostille-eligible.

faqs.q: Can I use a Basic DBS instead of an ACRO certificate?
faqs.a: Vietnam's decree only asks for a criminal record from the competent foreign authority and names no UK product. Whether the Ho Chi Minh City work-permit office accepts a Basic DBS is not published, so ask your employer before you order; both can only get a paper apostille.

faqs.q: Does a TEFL certificate replace the degree if my degree is hard to authenticate?
faqs.a: No. The degree and the experience proof are the work-permit test; the TEFL, TESOL or CELTA certificate meets the separate education rule. Both need authenticating and a certified translation.
